import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_3/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_3/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_3/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source3_3_2 and Source3_3_1 on movie_id
join_1 = pd.merge(source2, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Step 2: Join Source3_3_0 and the result of Step 1 on user_id
join_2 = pd.merge(join_1, source0, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema:
# Target schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float]

# Ensure movie_id is integer type
join_2["movie_id"] = join_2["movie_id"].astype(int)

# Select columns in target order
Target3_3 = join_2[["title", "user_id", "age", "occupation", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp"]]

# Save the final target table to the specified path
Target3_3.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_3_2 and Source3_3_1 on movie_id
joined_0 = pd.merge(source2, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join Source3_3_0 and the previous join on user_id
joined_1 = pd.merge(source0, joined_0, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns in target schema that are unique identifiers:
# title (string), user_id (float but used as identifier), age (float), occupation (float), movie_id (int)
# Aggregate rating and timestamp by mean to match target averages and reduce duplicates
result = joined_1.groupby(
    ["title", "user_id", "age", "occupation", "movie_id"], as_index=False
).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean"
})

# Ensure column order and names exactly as target schema
result = result[["title", "user_id", "age", "occupation", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp"]]

# Write to target file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
